pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound revealing a mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) in the right ovary, accompanied by CSF antibodies targeting the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: This auto-immune condition occurs when the immune system produces IgG antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in the central nervous system. In young female patients, the disease is frequently triggered by neural tissue within a pelvic teratoma. The host immune system recognizes these ectopic neural antigens as foreign, mounting an antibody response that crosses the blood-brain barrier. The antibodies bind and internalize neuronal NMDA receptors, leading to synaptic dysfunction, psychosis, movement disorders, autonomic collapse, and central hypoventilation. Treatment requires tumor resection alongside aggressive immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, steroids).
